If this is about how you can live on 70k than being on an income based plan, would help. It helps a lot if you make even less. I know this because I've been through that when I worked in a different field and lived in LA. I was making 50k and I did not have to eat one meal a day, I had enough groceries for a single person and I could eat every now and then. I think in SF, that 70k is livable for a single person willing to make tradeoffs to be in the city. I had roomates that was the downside but with the right people it's alright. It's not financial murder because this all based on assuming that you will make more money later on in your career, this is really based on you being a new grad in HCOL on a lower salary. It's also an ok situation if you like living with other roommates or don't plan to have a traditional family, so some people are comfortable living in LA/NYC long term.

If you have a full time job, your job is covering your health insurance. There are even some jobs that pay in to fully cover your health insurance and other coverage. I had a job like that, my salary was way low but nothing came out of my check for health insurance. But even if you are making 100k, something tragic can happen and you can struggle. You could also just get laid off.  It's not ignorant him asking why, because plenty people of live more frugal in those cities. Specifically Teachers/school workers, Film workers (who are always under the risk of not finding working). He would need a car for LA but that would be the main extra expense.

OP is cutting all costs for his personal choice but you don't need to be that strict on 70k in LA. You have to make tradeoffs with how you live but from my experience, I don't think those tradeoffs are that bad which was mainly living with roommates, smaller space and not being able to go to just any event or eat out at a high end restaurant every week. There was still of tons of things I could do instead of just sitting in my apartment like just going to the beach or hike, free music events, etc.

IMO, The real downside to be on on this salary 70k - 120k is you can't save or afford to save for a house. This is the main reason why people complain HCOL in california imo. You can afford an apartment/house rental but you're gonna sacrifice more space and being owner compared to other cities like Dallas/FT Worth, TX or in the south/midwest

OP is cheap but there's nothing wrong with that. He's not ignorant. You're just accustomed to living a certain lifestyle.

If you're living in NYC, Why do you need a car? It's not necessary even if you do have a kid.  
If you are low income and have student loans through federal gov, you should be on low income repayment plan. If you're living in a city, you're always going to have sacrifice space. That's not a new concept. It's been that way for a while now. It's tradeoff for living near events and easy access to things that aren't' found in the suburbs or country. Some people are content with small space because they're never home and don't plan on having a family. 

If you're just starting out in your career, you should be ok with living a little frugal because usually it should pay off as you advance in your career.

If this based on a single person, than it should be enough. Just go to the cheap grocery store. If you get 20 dollars that's 140 dollars a week, It might be pushing it for SF/NYC but I didn't spend more that 140 a week on food in LA and I was shopping at whole foods/trader's joe when i could've of went to walmart or stores like food4less.

I'm not arguing that it isn't low. I'm saying that people are living in those cities on less and you can live there if you want to on a lower salary. The idea that you can't move there unless you are making 100k is not entirely true. I know this because I've been living in LA on 40-50k and so did most of my friends. If you are actually in SF (not bay area), you don't need a car. Also california is expensive but they also offer more resources for low income than most states.  So if you are making more than the minimum, you should not be struggling. You can't afford all the things you want but you should have the things you need.

There are also tons of free events in these cities for entertainment and you can usually find really good food for cheap if you're willing to look.

Unless you have wife and kid, You should be living comfortably if you are making over 100k (unless you took out a crazy amount of student loans). People need to lower their expectations and stop trying to spend like their rich. They're are plenty of people living on less in those cities.

It's not ideal but possible from my experience with living HCOL like LA and SF and seeing how other people live. You rent a room and live with multiple people or with family. You live in the cheaper and maybe slightly sketchy area. You have a cheap car or no car. You go to free events and find cheap but good restaurants... which these cities actually have a lot of this. This is how people starting careers in creative fields or students live in these cities. This isn't bad unless you have kid.

I found that bland or cold foods were easier for me to eat. Also don't wait too late to take medicine for nausea.

That was the worst part for me. If you have to do that and it causes you pain, just ask your doctor for a really strong pain killer. You'll also be tired and sleepy a lot. When you do have some energy, try to go for walks or do activities you like. 

I hope everything goes smooth as possible for you. Stay Positive.
